What are some of the most infamous gaps in the Interstate Highway System that you know of.
Can you provide an example? I'm not sure i know what you mean. I guess it could be a case of, "If you don't know what I mean, you haven't seen it."

A Gap in an Interstate Highway would be when:

  1. There is a physical gap in an interstate highway where one part of the route doesn't have a direct connection to the rest of the route. Interstate 95 in Mercer County, NJ would be an example of this because the Southern part of I-95 does not have a direct connection to the northern part.

  2. One part of the interstate has a portion where the freeway temporarily ends and you may be forced to stop for an obstacle such as a movable bridge or traffic light. Interstate 70 in Breezewood, PA would be an example of this because when the Interstate needs to join a biplex with US-30 to connect back to I-70 on the PA turnpike, several traffic lights are required to be gone through before you can get to the other side of I-70.

  3. An interstate has too narrow lanes, no median to separate opposing traffic and/or the interstate only has one lane going each direction. Interstate 93 in Franconia Park, New Hampshire would be an example of this because certain parts of it only have one lane going a certain direction.

  4. A 3 digit Interstate never connects with its 2 digit parent. Interstate 278 in New York City would be an example of this because it never connects with Interstate 78.

Jiu Xing was almost at Yicun. She could see the light of the settlement in the distance. Still, she felt regret for doing what she did, running away from her family when she was told strictly not to go to the base camps. Her hands were starting to give out from carrying the wagon for so long, when she heard the noise of an animal in pain.

Just behind some shrubbery was a Landwalker with a twisted leg. What was worse is that a Direwolf was ready to strike it. Jiu took the bow and arrows from the wagon. She aimed directly at the Direwolf, and shot.

*Pft*

Direct hit into the shoulder!

The Direwolf let out a piercing screech and ran away, just before turning to see the one who shot it.

The Landwalker turned to Jiu. Its eyes were that of a creature that knew their fate was sealed, but was scared to death to accept it. Jiu crouched down by it and pet it, calming it down. She took nearby branches and leaves, tied it together with rope, and created a splint for its leg. The Landwalker, with help from Jiu, got up onto its feet once again. At first it waited for the sharp pain when it put pressure onto the twisted leg, but there was none.

The Landwalker grunted cheerfully, and rested its head against Jiu, trying to show its thanks. Jiu got up and began walking back to Yicun, when the Landwalker began following her. She ushered it to go elsewhere, but it was fruitless.

Jiu's kindness to the Landwalker had manged to score her a companion for her journey.
